paper.title: Design of a Neural Network to Predict Team Performance in Acute Ischemic Stroke
paper.version: author-hosted PDF, 5 pages, no journal/DOI printed

claims.text: The optimized network achieved precision 63%, recall 67%, F1 0.64 and accuracy 60% on the validation set.
claims.location: Abstract Results, p.1; Results, p.4; Table 2, p.5

claims.text: With four weakly associated parameters (duration, NIHSS severity, age, hour of day) the neural network constructed a reasonable prediction model for stroke team performance.
The four features individually show only weak association with door-to-needle time.
A 45-minute door-to-needle cut-off showed the best predictive performance and was used as the classification threshold.
Hyperparameters (learning rate 0.15, layer sizes 4-6-1, L2 lambda 0.02) were selected by systematic tuning.
The network was trained on 221 cases (2003-201x) and validated on 61 cases (last two years).
Application of a neural network to optimize acute stroke care with a predictive model is feasible and may improve team performance.

findings.location: Results, p.4, Table 2, p.5 vs Abstract Results, p.1
findings.evidence: 'F1 (validation)' differs and units differ (fraction vs %); could not convert automatically. Results, p.4: 0.64 fraction | Abstract Results, p.1: 64 % Ratio is 10^2: possible unit-mismatch, needs verification.
findings.question_for_authors: Is F1 reported as a fraction (0.64) or as a percentage (64%)? Please use one unit consistently.

findings.evidence: With the paper's own choices the claim 'The network reaches precision >= 63% and recall >= 67% on the validation set (the paper's reported performance)' does not hold on re-run (effect -0.986). Note: our re-run is a numpy port (substitute=true); the authors' stored output does match the paper, so this is reported as a port_gap in the reproduction gate and the multiverse robustness is measured around our re-run, not around the paper's number.
findings.question_for_authors: Please report the random seed and the exact TensorFlow version used, so the reported run can be reproduced.

findings.evidence: No dependency specification found (requirements.txt, environment.yml, renv.lock, ...). The capsule Dockerfile pins tensorflow:1.4.0-python2.7.12-cuda8.0.61-cudnn6.0.21-ubuntu16.04, but no Python-level requirements file is present.
findings.question_for_authors: Which exact numpy/TensorFlow versions were used, and can a requirements file be added?

findings.evidence: [G2] Are inclusion/exclusion rules stated, with counts removed at each step? -> not_reported. No inclusion/exclusion criteria and no counts removed before the 221/61 split.
findings.question_for_authors: What were the inclusion/exclusion criteria, and how many records were removed at each step before the 221/61 split?

findings.evidence: [G4] Is the outlier definition and removal rule stated (and applied before or after splitting)? -> not_reported. No outlier rule; nn.py uses all rows as given.
findings.question_for_authors: Were any outlier records removed, and if so by which rule and before or after the split?

findings.evidence: [M1] Are random seeds stated, and are results reported over several seeds? -> not_reported. No seed in paper or code; single run reported.
findings.question_for_authors: What random seed was used, and what is the spread of the reported metrics over several seeds?

findings.evidence: [M8] Were baselines given comparable tuning effort and the same data? -> not_reported. No baseline model (logistic regression, clinical score) reported.
findings.question_for_authors: How does the network compare with a logistic regression or a simple clinical rule on the same 61 validation cases?

findings.evidence: [M10] If the paper credits specific features or descriptors for the performance, is there a negative control (random or shuffled features, one-hot identity encoding, y-randomisation)? -> not_reported.
findings.question_for_authors: Was a negative control (shuffled labels or random features) run to show the network learns signal rather than noise?

findings.evidence: [M2] Is the validation set used for model selection, and is a separate test set held out? -> partial. The paper calls the 61 cases a validation set and also reports its metrics as final performance; hyperparameters were tuned on the same set.
findings.question_for_authors: Were the reported metrics obtained on data that was also used for hyperparameter selection?

findings.location: Abstract Results p.1 / Results p.4 / Table 2 p.5 vs results/predict-output.txt
findings.evidence: Paper reports precision 63, recall 67, F1 0.64, accuracy 60; the authors' stored output results/predict-output.txt prints PRECISION 62%, RECALL 66%, F1 62%, ACCURACY 60%. Recounting the stored prediction vector against data/test_data.csv rows 1-60 gives TP 22 / FP 13 / FN 11 / TN 14 = precision 62.86, recall 66.67, F1 64.71, accuracy 60.00, which matches the paper. The stored file's own printed F1 (62) does not match its own counts (64.71).
findings.question_for_authors: Which F1 value is correct for the validation set: 62 (printed in predict-output.txt) or 64.71 (recomputed from the same predictions)?

findings.location: Results p.4 and Table 2 p.5 vs results/predict-output.txt (EQUAL / TOTAL)
findings.evidence: predict-output.txt prints EQUAL 36 of TOTAL 60 (accuracy 60%). Recounting the same 60 predictions against data/test_data.csv rows 1-60 gives 30 equal (accuracy 50.00%). The 60% accuracy in the paper therefore cannot be reproduced from the stored prediction vector and the released labels.
findings.question_for_authors: Which 60 rows were scored, and can the scoring script that produced EQUAL=36 be released?

findings.location: Methods p.2 (61 validation cases) vs results/predict-output.txt (TOTAL 60)
findings.evidence: Methods state 61 validation cases; data/test_data.csv has 61 rows; the stored output scores TOTAL 60. One case is unaccounted for.
findings.question_for_authors: Why does the stored output score 60 cases when the validation set has 61?

findings.location: Hyperparameter tuning p.4 vs results/Output (220-row block)
findings.evidence: results/Output contains a 220-row prediction block whose printed metrics (precision 68, recall 69, F1 68, accuracy 65, EQUAL 145) do not match the paper's reported validation metrics (63/67/0.64/60). Recounting that block gives precision 68.03, recall 69.75, F1 68.88, accuracy 65.91 (TP 83 / FP 39 / FN 36 / TN 62). The paper does not report this 220-case result.
findings.question_for_authors: What is the 220-row block in results/Output, and why are its metrics not reported in the paper?

findings.location: Training p.3 / Hyperparameter tuning p.4 vs code/nn.py
findings.evidence: The paper describes systematic hyperparameter tuning; code/nn.py contains a single fixed configuration (learning rate 0.15, layers 4-6-1, lambda 0.02, 1500 iterations) with no tuning loop, and validation_sz = int(M_app*0.5) = 30 inside the training file.
findings.question_for_authors: Where is the hyperparameter search implemented, and on which data was it run?

findings.evidence: The paper states that a 45-minute cut-off showed the best predictive performance, but no code, table or figure compares alternative cut-offs, and the released CSV contains only the binary label (no raw door-to-needle minutes).
findings.question_for_authors: Which cut-offs were compared, and can the raw door-to-needle times be released so the comparison can be repeated?

findings.evidence: Neither the paper nor code/nn.py sets a random seed (no tf.set_random_seed / np.random.seed); a single run is reported. Our 5-seed re-run of the same pipeline gives validation accuracy 44.26-57.38% and precision 50.0-60.53%.
findings.question_for_authors: What seed produced the reported run, and what is the metric distribution over 50 seeds?

findings.location: Results p.4 / Table 2 p.5 (F1 0.64) and Hyperparameter tuning p.4 (F1 68)
findings.evidence: F1 is reported as 0.64 for the validation set and as 68 for the tuned configuration; with precision 63 and recall 67 the harmonic mean is 64.9, so 0.64 and 68 cannot both describe the same run.
findings.question_for_authors: Which run does F1 = 68 belong to?

findings.location: Hyperparameter tuning p.4 vs Results p.4
findings.evidence: Hyperparameters were selected using the same 61 cases whose metrics are reported as final performance; no separate held-out test set is described. The reported validation metrics are therefore optimistic.
findings.question_for_authors: Was any data held out from hyperparameter selection?

findings.location: bp_work/adapter.py (numpy port of code/nn.py, 5 seeds 0-4) vs results/predict-output.txt
findings.evidence: Our numpy port gives validation precision 55.02% (range 50.0-60.53) against the paper's 63%; the authors' stored output matches the paper, so this is our port's problem, not a paper finding.

findings.location: bp_work/adapter.py (numpy port of code/nn.py, 5 seeds 0-4) vs results/predict-output.txt
findings.evidence: Our numpy port gives validation F1 57.59 (range 51.52-63.89) against the paper's 0.64; stored output matches the paper.

findings.location: bp_work/adapter.py (numpy port of code/nn.py, 5 seeds 0-4) vs results/predict-output.txt
findings.evidence: Our numpy port gives validation accuracy 50.49% (range 44.26-57.38) against the paper's 60%; stored output matches the paper.
Recount of the stored 60-row block gives precision 62.86 against the printed 62 (rounding of the same counts).
Recount of the stored 60-row block gives recall 66.67 against the printed 66 (rounding of the same counts).
Recount of the stored 60-row block gives F1 64.71 against the printed 62 (the printed value is not the harmonic mean of its own counts).
Recount of the 220-row block gives recall 69.75 against the printed 69 (rounding).
Recount of the 220-row block gives F1 68.88 against the printed 68 (rounding).
Recount of the 220-row block gives accuracy 65.91 against the printed 65 (rounding).
[G1] Is the data source and collection period stated with counts per centre? -> partial. Ten stroke centres are mentioned but no per-centre counts are given.
findings.question_for_authors: How many cases came from each of the ten stroke centres?

findings.evidence: [G3] Is missing data handled and reported? -> not_reported. No missing-value statement; the released CSV has no missing cells, so the handling of missing values in the full cohort is unknown.
findings.question_for_authors: How were missing values in the source records handled before the 221/61 split?

findings.evidence: [G5] Is the split temporal or random, and is it stated? -> partial. The paper says the last two years were used for validation, but the released files carry no dates, so the split cannot be verified.
findings.question_for_authors: Can the case dates be released so the temporal split can be verified?

findings.evidence: [G6] Is the sample size justified (events per variable)? -> not_reported. 221 cases with 4 predictors and a 4-6-1 network; no power or EPV discussion.
findings.question_for_authors: How was the sample size of 221 cases justified for a network with 4-6-1 weights?

findings.evidence: [M3] Is the hyperparameter search space and selection criterion stated? -> partial. Values are listed but the search space and criterion are not.
findings.question_for_authors: What search space and selection criterion were used for the hyperparameters?

findings.evidence: The 45-minute cut-off comparison is shown only in a figure; no underlying data or code is released, so the claim cannot be checked.
findings.question_for_authors: Can the data behind Figure 1 be released?

findings.evidence: Table 1 reports univariate associations of the four features; no test statistics or CIs are given and the raw data behind the table are not released in a form that reproduces it.
findings.question_for_authors: Which test produced the associations in Table 1, and what are the effect sizes and CIs?

findings.evidence: The collection period is written as '2003-201x' in the paper; the exact end year is not reported.
findings.question_for_authors: What is the exact end year of the data collection period?

findings.evidence: The claim that the model may improve team performance is a projection; no prospective or interventional evaluation is reported.
findings.question_for_authors: Has the model been evaluated prospectively in the stroke pathway?

findings.evidence: The statement that 45 minutes is the guideline target is supported only by citation; the guideline text is not part of the materials.
Generalisation to other centres is asserted without external validation data.
findings.question_for_authors: Is there any external validation cohort?

findings.evidence: 3 quantities agree across the paper's own locations (abstract, results text, Table 2) after unit normalisation.
Sample sizes are consistent across locations: 221 training cases and 61 validation cases appear in Methods and match the released CSV row counts (221 and 61).

top_experiment.title: Re-run the released pipeline with 50 seeds and report the distribution of validation metrics
